mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES implies broader out-of-home activity is recovering, and that recovery should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as errands and discretionary trips spill back into shopping areas.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES continue improving for four weeks but RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines versus the prior four-week mean, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while TRANSIT remains depressed, households substitute away from shopping trips and retail visits fall within one to two weeks; the current gap should therefore keep RETAIL_REC below the previous four-week level.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +5 while TRANSIT below -15 for at least one week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 and TRANSIT remains below -15 for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above the last four-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below its recent already-low level signals tighter access or weaker commuting, and that shock propagates into retail traffic with a one-week lag, pushing RETAIL_REC down.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week from an already negative base
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls by more than 3 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility relative to its recent trough indicates improved outdoor weekend activity and softer avoidance behavior, which should feed through to higher discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below the last four-week average over the next month, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise together, commuting density increases and retail demand follows with a two-week lag because workers combine travel with lunch and after-work purchases.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior four-week mean within two weeks, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp improvement in GROCERY_PHARM above zero indicates normalization of essential errand behavior, and that easing of caution typically precedes a broader retail rebound within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to non-negative
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses into non-negative territory but RETAIL_REC stays below its last four-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -20 while WORKPLACES also stays below -20, the city is still operating under a mobility-constrained regime and retail demand will keep weakening over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -20 and WORKPLACES below -20 simultaneously
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below -20 for four weeks but RETAIL_REC rises above the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The recent narrowing gap between RESIDENTIAL and out-of-home categories signals people are spending slightly less time at home and slightly more time outside; that pattern should produce a modest retail lift within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while both PARKS and TRANSIT rise in the same week
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls and PARKS plus TRANSIT rise in the same week but RETAIL_REC does not improve the following week, the hypothesis fails.
